title: Lead with duplicate detection as a differentiator against VaultSweep
rationale: VaultSweep's verified feature_duplicates value is 'no', so duplicate-file detection is a concrete point where CacheDrop can stand out in comparisons. Build it into the headline feature set and marketing copy. Base this on the verified 'no' only; do not infer anything about other competitors.

title: Compete on transparent one-time pricing in the same model
rationale: VaultSweep is also one-time priced at $24.99 sold direct. Since CacheDrop shares the one-time model, the comparison will turn on value and clarity, not on the model itself. Make the one-time price and what it includes easy to see at the point of purchase.

title: Evaluate a free trial to match the category norm set by VaultSweep
rationale: VaultSweep offers a 7-day free trial. For a one-time purchase, a trial lets users check that cleanup and uninstall work on their own machines (large sample libraries, plug-in folders, render caches) before paying. Consider offering one to remove this as a reason to choose VaultSweep.

title: Position on producer, developer and editor workflows rather than generic space recovery
rationale: VaultSweep's headline 'Reclaim gigabytes of space.' is a generic storage message. CacheDrop's audience is music producers, developers and video editors. Write headlines around their specific pain points. VaultSweep also lists developer cleanup as a feature, so the niche claim has to rest on depth of workflow fit, not on developer cleanup alone.
